title: 2nd Abyss And The Means For Escaping 1st Matter The Narrow Minds Denial Of Grandeur And The Impossibility Of Unbelief

questions.question: What is the main danger described in the Second Abyss?
questions.answer: It is the danger of falling into unbelief and going astray because a person’s mind and heart become too limited to understand great truths.

questions.question: What can make a person’s understanding become narrow in this passage?
questions.answer: Being deeply caught in forgetting Allah, sin, and only material things can make understanding narrow.

questions.question: Why do some people rush to deny great truths?
questions.answer: They do it because they feel proud of the little knowledge they have and cannot grasp bigger matters.

questions.question: What kinds of faith matters are said to be too great for these narrowed minds?
questions.answer: They are very vast, deep, and wide truths of belief.

questions.question: Besides the intellect, what other part of a person is described as being in bad shape?
questions.answer: The heart is described as spoiled and spiritually lifeless.

questions.question: What happens when people cannot fit the truths of faith into their limited thinking?
questions.answer: They fall into unbelief and misguidance and become overwhelmed.

questions.question: If such people looked honestly at their unbelief, what would they notice?
questions.answer: They would see that it hides many foolish and impossible ideas.

questions.question: How is belief compared to unbelief in terms of reason?
questions.answer: Belief is shown as reasonable, fitting, and even necessary, while unbelief leads to nonsense and impossibilities.

questions.question: What wrong idea is given as an example about someone who refuses Allah’s necessary existence and eternal nature?
questions.answer: Such a person may wrongly spread Allah’s qualities among countless beings or endless tiny particles.

questions.question: What extreme example is given about the Sophists?
questions.answer: They are described as becoming so mistaken that they deny both themselves and the world around them.

questions.question: How do the truths of belief and Islam stay safe from the false ideas of unbelief?
questions.answer: They rely on the greatness and highness that belong to them.

questions.question: Where do the truths of belief settle firmly in the end?
questions.answer: They settle in healthy hearts and upright minds through full submission and acceptance.

questions.question: How many parts are mentioned in the way out of the Second Abyss?
questions.answer: Two parts are mentioned.

questions.question: What is discussed in the first part of that escape?
questions.answer: It explains how limited minds and damaged hearts can lead people to denial.

questions.question: Which three things are named as causes of a narrowed mind?
questions.answer: Neglect of Allah, sin, and being absorbed in the material world.

questions.question: Why can these people not understand the truths of faith well?
questions.answer: Because the truths are too lofty, great, and endless for their shrunken understanding.

questions.question: What bad character trait pushes them toward denial?
questions.answer: Pride in their own small amount of knowledge pushes them toward denial.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the heart of such a person?
questions.answer: It says the heart is corrupted and spiritually dead or near dead.

questions.question: What is the result of using such a weak inner state to judge faith?
questions.answer: The person falls into unbelief, misguidance, and confusion.

questions.question: What would they learn if they examined unbelief carefully?
questions.answer: They would learn that unbelief contains many absurd and impossible ideas.

questions.question: What does the passage say has strongly shown this truth?
questions.answer: It says the Risale-i Nur has shown it through many comparisons with complete certainty.

questions.question: What false move is described when someone rejects Allah’s unique qualities?
questions.answer: He may wrongly give those qualities to unlimited creatures or infinite atoms.

questions.question: What lesson comes from the example of denying one’s own existence and the world’s existence?
questions.answer: It shows that unbelief can become so unreasonable that it makes a person give up clear thinking.

questions.question: According to the passage, what helps belief take its place in people?
questions.answer: Complete submission and willing acceptance help belief settle in sound hearts and straight minds.

questions.question: What kind of people are being warned about in this passage?
questions.answer: People whose minds are narrowed by sins, heedlessness, and too much focus on the physical world are being warned.

questions.question: What is wrong with the knowledge these people trust in so much?
questions.answer: It is small and limited, but they act as if it is enough for huge questions.

questions.question: Why is denial shown as a hasty action here?
questions.answer: Because people deny the truth quickly instead of admitting that their understanding is too small.

questions.question: What are the truths of faith like according to the passage?
questions.answer: They are grand, deep, wide, and beyond the reach of a dried-up mind.

questions.question: What does it mean that the heart is spiritually lifeless?
questions.answer: It means the heart is no longer healthy in faith and is not alive to spiritual truth.

questions.question: What is one major difference between belief and unbelief in this passage?
questions.answer: Belief matches greatness and truth, while unbelief hides foolishness and impossibility.

questions.question: Why is it unreasonable to spread Allah’s special qualities among endless beings?
questions.answer: Because those qualities belong properly to Allah alone, and giving them to countless beings creates impossible ideas.

questions.question: What does the example about denying oneself and the universe show about false thinking?
questions.answer: It shows that false thinking can become so extreme that it rejects things that are obvious.

questions.question: What kinds of bad things does belief protect people from?
questions.answer: It protects them from absurd ideas, scary false beliefs, and dark ignorance.

questions.question: What two places inside a person are made ready to receive the truths of Islam?
questions.answer: A healthy heart and a straight mind are made ready.

questions.question: What personal quality helps a person accept the truths of belief?
questions.answer: Humble submission and sincere acceptance help a person accept them.

questions.question: What causes some minds to become too tight to understand big truths?
questions.answer: Forgetting Allah, committing sins, and being overly tied to material things cause that problem.

questions.question: What kind of truths are too big for these restricted minds?
questions.answer: The truths of faith, which are lofty, huge, and far-reaching, are too big for them.

questions.question: How does pride harm a person in this passage?
questions.answer: Pride makes a person trust limited knowledge too much and quickly reject what is greater.

questions.question: What happens to people when their minds and hearts are not healthy enough for faith’s truths?
questions.answer: They throw themselves into unbelief and wrong guidance and become trapped.

questions.question: What would a fair look at unbelief uncover?
questions.answer: It would uncover many ideas that do not make sense and cannot truly be.

questions.question: How certain is the proof said to be in showing this problem?
questions.answer: It is presented as being as certain as a very clear math fact.

questions.question: What is one example of a false belief described in the passage?
questions.answer: One example is giving Allah’s unique qualities to unlimited beings or endless atoms.

questions.question: Why is denying both oneself and the universe presented as foolish?
questions.answer: Because it rejects things that are plainly real and shows a person has abandoned sound thinking.

questions.question: What do the truths of belief and Islam rest on?
questions.answer: They rest on the greatness and majesty that properly belong to them.

questions.question: From what three harms do these truths free themselves?
questions.answer: They free themselves from absurd nonsense, frightening superstitions, and deep ignorance.

questions.question: Where do these truths finally take their place?
questions.answer: They take their place in sound hearts and straight intellects.

questions.question: By what attitude do people receive these truths properly?
questions.answer: They receive them through full submission and assent.

questions.question: In this passage, what keeps a person from understanding very great truths?
questions.answer: A narrowed mind caused by neglect of Allah, sin, and too much attachment to the material world keeps a person from understanding them.

questions.question: What mistake do such people make about their own knowledge?
questions.answer: They become proud of it even though it is too small for the matters they are judging.

questions.question: What is the connection between limited understanding and denial?
questions.answer: When people cannot grasp the truths of faith, they may start rejecting them.

questions.question: How are the minds of these deniers described?
questions.answer: They are described as cramped and dried out.

questions.question: How are their hearts described?
questions.answer: Their hearts are described as corrupt and nearly dead in a spiritual way.

questions.question: What does the passage say unbelief contains when compared with belief?
questions.answer: It contains many absurd and impossible claims.

questions.question: What is special about belief in that comparison?
questions.answer: Belief is shown as fitting, reasonable, and necessary.

questions.question: What wrong result can come from rejecting Allah’s necessary existence and eternal nature?
questions.answer: A person may wrongly hand Allah’s qualities over to countless beings or to endless tiny particles.

questions.question: What does the example of the Sophists teach?
questions.answer: It teaches that unbelief can become so extreme that a person denies even obvious existence.

questions.question: What shields the truths of Islam from the false ideas of unbelief?
questions.answer: Their own grandeur and sublimity shield them.

questions.question: What does unbelief confront belief with in this passage?
questions.answer: It confronts belief with absurdity, superstition, and ignorance.

questions.question: What kind of students of truth, based on this passage, are most ready to accept faith well?
questions.answer: Those with humble, healthy hearts and straight, balanced minds are most ready.

questions.question: What is the first matter in escaping the Second Abyss mainly about?
questions.answer: It is mainly about understanding why some people deny faith and how belief remains stronger and sounder.

questions.question: What three influences can shrink a person’s understanding?
questions.answer: Neglecting Allah, falling into sin, and being absorbed only in physical things can shrink it.

questions.question: Why do these people fail to understand the greatness of belief?
questions.answer: They fail because their minds have become too small to take in matters of greatness and endlessness.

questions.question: What feeling makes them quickly turn to denial instead of patience and learning?
questions.answer: Pride makes them quickly turn to denial.

questions.question: What inner condition makes their response even worse than simple lack of knowledge?
questions.answer: Their hearts are spiritually damaged, which makes their response worse.

questions.question: According to the passage, what would happen if they truly examined their own unbelief?
questions.answer: They would discover that it is full of unreasonable and impossible ideas.

questions.question: What example is given of replacing one true belief with a much stranger claim?
questions.answer: Rejecting Allah’s unique divine qualities and then spreading them among endless beings or atoms is given as an example.

questions.question: What is the lesson of the example about denying oneself and the universe?
questions.answer: The lesson is that unbelief can push a person into denying what is obvious and certain.

questions.question: What do all the truths of belief and Islam rely on?
questions.answer: They rely on the grandeur and sublimity that belong to them.

questions.question: What do those truths leave behind when they are accepted?
questions.answer: They leave behind the absurdity, superstition, and dark ignorance found in unbelief.

questions.question: In what kind of people do these truths find a proper home?
questions.answer: They find a home in sound hearts and straight intellects.

questions.question: What two attitudes are named as the way these truths are received?
questions.answer: Submission and assent are the two attitudes named.
